correctness.rationale: The local EFX inequality is proved iff by considering every deletion; uniform cycle violations correspond exactly to isolated sign runs. Heavy and light one-edge exceptions are separately identified and bijected by cyclic shifts. The explicit four-state matrix has characteristic polynomial \((x^2-x-1)(x^2-x+1)\), proving \(N_n(1)=L_n+2\cos(n\pi/3)\), while the marked ++ diagonal gives \(F_{n+1}\) plus a period-six correction for any nonunit edge. A constructed forbidden equal-weight word proves strict loss for every \(n\ge4\), and Binet asymptotics yield \(\varphi/\sqrt5\). Standalone brute force checked 81,880 labeled orientation-weight pairs and 98 matrix lengths; finite checking is corroboration only.

originality.rationale: Full text comparisons with original graphical EFX orientations and later EFX papers, plus six semantic mathematical-record queries, did not identify a theorem enumerating symmetric positive cycle EFX orientations after perturbing one edge or quantifying the asymptotically nonzero fraction lost. Standard forbidden-pattern counts and known bipartite EFX existence do not alone imply the one-defect heavy/light equality. Published four-cycle equal-weight census covers only a baseline subcase. Undiscovered equivalent special-case enumerations remain possible.
residual_risks: Unindexed weighted orientation counting or elementary transfer-matrix literature may contain an equivalent formula.
The novelty claim is about the one-edge EFX count sensitivity, not a new Fibonacci/Lucas sequence identity.
Searches are evidence of noncoverage of checked work, not a mathematical proof of global novelty.

value.rationale: For one of the simplest relevant fair-division graph models, exact EFX-allocation prevalence is discontinuously sensitive to an arbitrarily small positive one-edge valuation change. The proved all-size sharp \(27.64\%\) asymptotic loss, plus symmetry of overweight/underweight perturbations and complete exact census, motivates and resolves a natural stability question beyond a small instance.
